title: Development and Validation of Quantitative Real-Time PCR for Detection of CHO Host Cell DNA
author: Zheng, Jiang, et al.
materials: CHO Genomic DNA was extracted from fresh CHO-k1 cell cultures using the QIAamp® DNA Mini kit(Qiagen, Germany)according to manufacturer’s protocol including RNAse lysis step. Eluted DNA was quantified by UV spectrophotometry at an absorbance of 260 nm and 280 nm and it was stored at − 20 °C for later use.

steps.title: Prepare CHO genomic DNA standard
steps.instruction: Extract CHO‑k1 genomic DNA using the QIAamp® DNA Mini kit (Qiagen, Germany) following the manufacturer’s protocol, including the RNase lysis step; quantify the eluted DNA by UV spectrophotometry at 260 nm and 280 nm; store the DNA at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: Dilute protein sample and spike with DNA
steps.instruction: Take 150 µL of protein sample, dilute it three‑fold with TE buffer (pH 6–8) to keep the pH within the activity range of Proteinase K; optionally add 10 µL of the CHO DNA standard to create spiked samples; prepare a negative control containing 450 µL TE buffer.

steps.title: Digest proteins with Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of Proteinase K (2 mg/mL, Sangon Biotech, China) to each tube (samples, spiked samples, and negative control) and incubate at 60 °C for 60 minutes.

steps.title: Precipitate residual DNA with co‑precipitant
steps.instruction: To each tube add 5 µL Pellet Paint® Co‑Precipitant (Merck, Germany), 50 µL 5 M NaCl, and 500 µL isopropanol (Sinopharm Chemical Reagent, China); mix and let stand at room temperature for 5 minutes; then centrifuge at 12 000 rpm for 10 minutes to pellet the DNA.

steps.title: Wash, dry and resuspend DNA for qPCR
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet with 70 % ethanol (Sinopharm Chemical Reagent, China) and centrifuge again at 12 000 rpm for 8 minutes; air‑dry the pellet at room temperature for 30 minutes; finally dissolve the DNA in TE buffer and proceed to quantitative real‑time PCR.
